title: Hilbert convolution for a normally flat ideal with regular quotient
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal. Put $A=R/I$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/I$ and $k=R/\mathfrak m=A/\mathfrak n$. Assume that $A$ is a regular local ring of dimension $s\geq0$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Form
$$G=\operatorname{gr}_I R=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}I^j/I^{j+1},\qquad F=G\otimes_Ak$$
[def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and assume that $G$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Each $F_j=(I^j/I^{j+1})\otimes_Ak$ is finite-dimensional over $k$; set $h_j=\dim_kF_j$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Then, for every integer $n\geq0$,
$$\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n}h_j\binom{n-j+s}{s}$$
with length as in [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. No reducedness, coefficient field, excellence or completeness hypothesis is imposed; $I=0$ and $I=\mathfrak m$ are allowed.

source.place: Ancestor motivation only: ILO VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94. Precise ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), section 2, printed p.153, and the paragraph after Example (4.2), printed p.157: the normal-flat tangent-cone product gives the numerical convolution. This node states only that numerical local-algebra consequence, including the passage to a regular ambient presentation after completion in the general Noetherian local case. Original cited there: Resolution of singularities (1964), Chapter II, Theorem 2. https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival source WANTED. No Stacks tag states this normal-flat Hilbert formula.

proof.text: Write $G_j=I^j/I^{j+1}$. By [lem-trf-flat-graded-fibre-regular-lift] every $G_j$ is finite free over $A$. Choose an $A$-basis of $G_j$. Tensoring its basis expansion with $k$ identifies $F_j$ with $k^{r_j}$, where $r_j$ is the number of basis vectors; thus $r_j=h_j$, including $r_j=0$. Choose a minimal generating list $\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_s$ of $\mathfrak n$ and lifts $y_i\in\mathfrak m$; the definition of regular local ring gives its length $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] the list is regular on $A$. On each $G_j\simeq A^{h_j}$, its successive multiplication maps are direct sums of those on $A/(\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_{i-1})$, hence injective. Put $J=(y_1,\ldots,y_s)$. Since the images generate $\mathfrak m/I$, one has $\mathfrak m=I+J$.

source.place: Tag 00NZ, lemma-finite-flat-local; Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM. Normal-flat graded freeness is supplied by the cited existing node.

proof.text:
For each $a\geq0$, the ideal $I^a$ is a finite $R$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], applied inside the finite module $R$. Its $I$-adic graded piece in degree $p$ is $I^{a+p}/I^{a+p+1}=G_{a+p}$, so Step 1 checks all the successive multiplication-injectivity hypotheses for the parameters $y_i$. Apply [lem-trf-adic-degree-zero-regular-strict-powers] to $M=I^a$. It gives, inside $I^a$ and hence inside $R$,
$$J^qI^a\cap I^{a+p}=J^q I^{a+p}\qquad(a,p,q\geq0).$$
In particular this applies with $p=1$; it also covers $I^a=0$.

source.place: Strict-power lemma applied to every shifted I-adic filtration; finite ideals by Noetherianity.

proof.text:
For $N\geq j$, expand $\mathfrak m^N=(I+J)^N=\sum_{a=0}^N I^aJ^{N-a}$. Let $z\in I^j\cap\mathfrak m^N$ and choose such a sum representation. Eliminate the terms indexed by $a<j$ in increasing order. After the earlier terms have been absorbed, write $z=u_a+\sum_{b>a}u_b$, with $u_a\in I^aJ^{N-a}$ and the tail contained in $I^{a+1}$. Since $z\in I^j\subseteq I^{a+1}$, Step 2 gives
$$u_a\in J^{N-a}I^a\cap I^{a+1}=J^{N-a}I^{a+1}\subseteq I^{a+1}J^{N-a-1}.$$
Thus absorb $u_a$ into the next term. Induction on $a=0,\ldots,j-1$ leaves a representation using only terms with $a\geq j$. Modulo $I^{j+1}$ only the $a=j$ term survives. Conversely $I^jJ^{N-j}\subseteq I^j\cap\mathfrak m^N$. Hence the image of $I^j\cap\mathfrak m^N$ in $G_j$ is precisely $\mathfrak n^{N-j}G_j$. The argument for $j=0$ has no elimination steps. We only assert equality of these images, not equality of the intersection with its single lowest term.

source.place: Elementary finite induction on the ideal-sum expansion, using the strict intersections of Step 2.

proof.text:
Fix $n\geq0$, put $N=n+1$, and filter $R/\mathfrak m^N$ by $L_j=(I^j+\mathfrak m^N)/\mathfrak m^N$, $0\leq j\leq N$. Then $L_0=R/\mathfrak m^N$ and $L_N=0$ since $I^N\subseteq\mathfrak m^N$. For $0\leq j<N$, the map $I^j\to L_j/L_{j+1}$ is onto and its kernel is
$$I^{j+1}+(I^j\cap\mathfrak m^N)=I^{j+1}+J^{N-j}I^j.$$
Indeed, if $z\in I^j$ belongs to $I^{j+1}+\mathfrak m^N$, write $z=u+v$ with $u\in I^{j+1}$; then $v=z-u\in I^j\cap\mathfrak m^N$. Consequently
$$L_j/L_{j+1}\simeq G_j/\mathfrak n^{N-j}G_j\simeq(A/\mathfrak n^{N-j})^{h_j}.$$
The action of $J$ on $G_j$ is that of $\mathfrak n$, so these are isomorphisms of $R$-modules via $R\to A$.

source.place: Elementary quotient-kernel calculation using Step 3; no identification of a filtered ring with its graded ring is asserted.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] to the parameters of $A$ from Step 1. It identifies $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}A$ with $k[Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$ by the specified parameter map. For $t\geq1$, filter $A/\mathfrak n^t$ by its powers of $\mathfrak n$. The successive factors have a $k$-basis consisting of the monomials of degrees $0,\ldots,t-1$. Each basis vector contributes one simple $R$-module $k$: its submodules are $k$-subspaces because $R\to k$ is surjective. Hence repeated [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] gives
$$\operatorname{length}_R(A/\mathfrak n^t)=\#\{\alpha\in\mathbf N^s:|\alpha|<t\}=\binom{t-1+s}{s}.$$
For the last count adjoin a slack coordinate $\alpha_{s+1}=t-1-|\alpha|$ and encode the resulting tuple of sum $t-1$ by $t-1$ stars and $s$ separators. There is one tuple if $s=0$. Direct sums of $h_j$ such modules have $h_j$ times this length, by the same length-additivity theorem applied to split exact sequences.

source.place: Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular; Tag 00IV, lemma-length-additive. The stars-and-bars count and residue-field composition series are written explicitly.

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] on $0\to L_{j+1}\to L_j\to L_j/L_{j+1}\to0$, starting at $L_N=0$. Steps 4 and 5 show all factors have finite length and give
$$\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n}h_j\binom{n-j+s}{s}.$$
This is the stated formula with the original residue-field fibre ranks. For $I=0$, only $G_0=A$ contributes. For $I=\mathfrak m$, the parameter list is empty and every binomial coefficient is $1$. At $n=0$ the sole summand is $h_0=1$. No coefficient-field section or completion was used.

proof_origin.place: Filtered-module proof of the numerical consequence motivating Hironaka (1970), pp.153,157; algebraic synthesis of Tags 00NZ, 00NQ, 00LN, 00IV and the strict-power lemma. The full numerical statement is not attributed to any Stacks tag.
